summary.headline: SpaceX buys Cursor for $60B as EU delays AI Act rules
summary.body: A busier day, led by consolidation. Days after its IPO, SpaceX, parent of xAI, agreed an all-stock deal to buy the AI coding firm Cursor for $60 billion. Fewer, bigger players means more Power Concentration, which feeds the endings where a single owner holds the keys: Enslaved God (a boxed super-AI owned by one lab), Zookeeper and Benevolent Dictator, while Libertarian Utopia, which needs power spread out, falls. China's Z.ai pushed the other way by releasing an open-weight GLM-5.2 model, which spreads capability around. In Europe, Parliament voted to push AI Act high-risk rules back to December 2027, and a report tied the US block on Anthropic models to a Korean telecom's alleged China links; both weaken Global Coordination and trim Gatekeeper. Horizon Balance: +1.50.
summary.movers_note: Enslaved God +0.4, Libertarian Utopia -0.3 and Zookeeper +0.3. The SpaceX-Cursor deal did most of the work (Enslaved God +0.48, Libertarian Utopia -0.48 from that event), partly offset by Z.ai's open-weight release (Libertarian Utopia +0.21).
coming_up: EU AI Act stand-alone high-risk obligations now due December 2027 (embedded products August 2028), per the Parliament vote

events.title: Report: Korean telecom's alleged China ties triggered US block on Anthropic models
events.summary: Citing the Washington Post, Korea JoongAng Daily reported the White House weighed controls after a Korean telecom 'suspected of ties to China' appeared among Mythos 5 access holders; SK Telecom declined to comment.
events.reason: Explains the national-security rationale behind the Jun 12 controls (China-leakage fear plus an Amazon-reported jailbreak); deepens tech decoupling.

events.title: SpaceX agrees to buy Cursor for $60 billion in stock
events.summary: Days after its IPO, SpaceX (parent of xAI) agreed an all-stock deal for AI coding firm Cursor, aiming to 'build the world's most useful AI models' on its Colossus compute.
events.reason: Big acquisition consolidating a frontier lab, compute and a top AI app (rubric T2 up).

events.title: Z.ai releases open-weight GLM-5.2; CEO says China will match Fable 5 soon
events.summary: China's Z.ai (Zhipu) released MIT-licensed GLM-5.2, reported to beat GPT-5.5 on several coding benchmarks at a fraction of the cost; founder Jie Tang said a Chinese Fable-5-class model is coming sooner than Musk's Q1 2027 estimate.
events.reason: Strong open-weights model narrows gap with US frontier (rubric T2 down for F5). Release date given as Jun 13 by some outlets, Jun 16 by Tom's Hardware.

events.title: European Parliament votes to delay EU AI Act high-risk rules
events.summary: Parliament adopted the AI 'digital omnibus', pushing stand-alone high-risk obligations from Aug 2026 to Dec 2027 (embedded products to Aug 2028) while adding a ban on AI-generated CSAM and non-consensual intimate imagery.
events.reason: Major regulator softens and postpones its flagship regime (partial rollback); offset slightly by new prohibitions.
